conceptZh: 短手橡膠恐龍用全身堆高橡膠外皮，踮腳補上一顆皮球後整塔倒塌，外皮落成「皮」字，只剩牠的眼睛從縫隙探出。
object: Five thick rubber outer-skin strips and one small rubber ball
morph: A precarious tower of rubber skin strips topples into the five correctly arranged strokes of 皮.
creativeAngle: 把橡膠外皮變成可堆疊的實體筆畫，讓短手恐龍用鼻尖、肚子和大腳忙亂施工；最後一顆小皮球壓垮高塔，同時完成倒塌笑點與詞語示範。
promptEn:
Create an 8-second stylized 3D cartoon with one original rubber dinosaur: enormous feet, absurdly tiny arms, a springy belly and an intensely determined grin. Use a fixed frontal camera, a pale apricot background and a shallow stage. Five thick, saturated cobalt rubber outer-skin strips have smooth molded surfaces and lighter undersides; their shapes correspond precisely to the five strokes of the Traditional Chinese glyph 皮. One small coral rubber ball is the only additional prop.

0.0–1.6 seconds: The dinosaur wants to crown its rubber-strip tower with the ball. It looks from the ball beside its foot to the growing stack, beams, and begins piling the strips using its nose and belly. Its tiny arms paddle uselessly. At 0.4 seconds, the off-screen voice says the first “皮” while a visibly flexible outer-skin strip bends over its nose and lands on the stack.

1.6–3.3 seconds: The dinosaur tries to lift the next strip with both tiny arms, misses completely, then scoops it up with an enormous foot and catches it on its snout. It stacks the remaining strips higher, rising onto tiptoe; every addition makes the tower sway farther. Finally it nudges the little ball up its belly and balances it on its nose, looking triumphantly upward.

3.3–4.8 seconds: It sets that tiny final ball on top. A brief frozen blink—then the tower leans, folds and tumbles forward with one soft rubber BONK. The impact spreads the five strips flat into a precisely formed 皮, using the standard five-stroke structure and exact intersections, with no extra marks. The dinosaur is briefly buried behind the fallen strips, only its blinking eyes visible through an open gap. The ball bounces clear to the lower-right margin. The second “皮” accompanies the final settling of the strokes, finishing at 4.8 seconds.

4.8–8.0 seconds: Hold the completed glyph perfectly still, centered, uncropped and about 70% of frame height. The dinosaur slides out from behind it into the lower-left margin and gives a dizzy grin. At 6.1 seconds, say “皮球” exactly as it gently belly-bumps the visible rubber ball into one springy bounce below the glyph. It finishes with a silent delighted foot wiggle, clear of every stroke.

Audio: warm, friendly off-screen Taiwanese Mandarin, slowly and distinctly, with clear tones. Speak exactly “皮、皮、皮球” (ㄆㄧˊ、ㄆㄧˊ、ㄆㄧˊ ㄑㄧㄡˊ), at the three specified picture cues; stop afterward. Use gentle squeaks and a soft impact, no music or extra dialogue. Only 皮 appears as text; no subtitles, logos, watermarks, clutter or flashing effects.
